text: [BLOCKER] No human genetic, transcriptomic, or genomic evidence exists anywhere in the platform; 13 of 14 named targets have no genetic support for the implied indication, and the 38 bio-database skills the repo vendors are all unused — The platform calls itself a 'state-of-the-art … artificial intelligence-driven drug discovery platform' (README.md:22) and presents 25 therapeutic candidates against ~17 distinct molecular targets, but contains zero human genetic evidence for any target-indication pair. Target selection appears to be driven entirely by traditional-medicine pharmacology narrative. I ran the analysis the platform omits. Open Targets Platform (api.platform.opentargets.org/api/v4, accessed 2026-08-16), Alzheimer disease = MONDO_0004975, overall association score and the genetic_association datatype score: TREM2 0.558 / genetic 0.862; NOS3 0.187 / genetic 0.278; NTRK2 0.124 / genetic 0.080; and for ACHE (0.641), GSK3B (0.554), GRIN2A (0.623), CHRNA7 (0.442), CHRM1 (0.409), NTRK1 (0.222), NFE2L2 (0.120), SLC1A2 (0.112), KEAP1 (0.088), PTAFR (0.085), FZD8 (0.002) the genetic_association datatype is ABSENT — the association scores are carried entirely by 'literature' (text-mined co-mention) and, for ACHE/GRIN2A/CHRM1/CHRNA7, by 'clinical' (i.e. the fact that donepezil/memantine/xanomeline-class drugs exist, which is circular). Benchmarks on the same query: APP 0.872 / genetic 0.923, APOE 0.770 / genetic 0.889. Scanning the top 200 associations for each target for the strongest genetic_association to ANY disease: TREM2's #2 is Alzheimer disease (0.86); no other platform target has AD anywhere in its genetic evidence. PTAFR has genetic evidence for exactly one disease in the whole Platform (hypothyroidism, 0.05). FZD8's AD literature score is 0.015 and its overall AD score is 0.002 — effectively indistinguishable from a random gene. Consequence: Genetic support is the single best-quantified predictor of clinical success available at the target-selection stage, and it is precisely the step this platform skips. On the Minikel 2024 relative-success figure of 2.6x with a ~10% base rate from Phase I to approval, and assuming a quarter of pipeline programmes are genetically supported, P(approval | genetic support) ≈ 18.6% versus ≈ 7.1% without — an absolute 11.4-point swing per programme. 1 of 17 distinct targets here (5.9%) carries genetic support for the implied indication, so the portfolio sits almost entirely on the low side of that split. Concretely: an investor, collaborator, or reviewer shown this platform would conclude that 25 candidates had passed a validation gate they never passed. The repo vendoring 38 genomics databases while wiring in none of them makes the gap worse, not better — it advertises a capability that does not exist, and any reader who checks the file tree will reasonably assume the data flowed into the platform.

text: Required fix for GENO-01: Add a genetics gate upstream of every candidate and make it visible in the UI. Minimum implementable specification: (1) For each target, call the Open Targets GraphQL API for the declared indication EFO/MONDO ID and store overall score plus the full datatypeScores breakdown; display genetic_association separately from literature and clinical, and refuse to display an overall score without the breakdown (the platform's own numbers show why: ACHE's 0.641 is 100% non-genetic). (2) Store, per target, the specific GWAS credible sets and the L2G / locus-to-gene assignment, plus any Mendelian/ClinVar coding evidence, with GWAS Catalog study accessions. (3) Add gnomAD v4 constraint (pLI, o/e LoF, LOEUF, missense Z) from gnomad.broadinstitute.org/api per target. (4) Where a continuous exposure exists (e.g. eNOS/NO, glutamate clearance), run or cite two-sample Mendelian randomization and eQTL/pQTL colocalization (coloc PP.H4) rather than asserting mechanism. (5) Wire the already-vendored skills — .agents/skills/opentargets-database, gnomad-database, gtex-database, clinvar-database, dbsnp-database, alphagenome-single-variant-analysis — into a build-time data-fetch step that emits a versioned JSON evidence file, and stamp each panel with the resource release version and access date. (6) Any target that fails the gate must be labelled 'no human genetic support — pharmacology hypothesis only' in the card UI, not silently ranked alongside TREM2.

tags: Human genetics & genomics — therapeutic target validation (GWAS, Mendelian randomization, QTL colocalization, population constraint)
text: Ground truth for GENO-01: Nelson et al., Nat Genet 47:856-60 (2015), DOI 10.1038/ng.3314: 'the proportion of drug mechanisms with direct genetic support increases significantly across the drug development pipeline, from 2.0% at the preclinical stage to 8.2% among mechanisms for approved drugs… selecting genetically supported targets could double the success rate in clinical development.' King, Davis & Degner, PLoS Genet 15:e1008489 (2019), DOI 10.1371/journal.pgen.1008489: 'When causal genes are clear (Mendelian traits and GWAS associations linked to coding variants), we find the use of human genetic evidence increases approval by greater than two-fold, and, for Mendelian associations, the positive association holds prospectively.' Minikel, Painter, Dong & Nelson, Nature 629:624-629 (2024), DOI 10.1038/s41586-024-07316-0: 'We estimate the probability of success for drug mechanisms with genetic support is 2.6 times greater than those without… largely unaffected by genetic effect size, minor allele frequency or year of discovery.' The correct evidence architecture for an AD/cognition target set is defined by Bellenguez et al., Nat Genet 54:412-436 (2022), DOI 10.1038/s41588-022-01024-z (75 AD/dementia risk loci from 111,326 cases and 677,663 controls, with 31 newly prioritized genes and microglial pathway enrichment) and is queryable programmatically via the Open Targets Platform (Ochoa et al., Nucleic Acids Res 51:D1353-D1359, 2023, DOI 10.1093/nar/gkac1046).

text: [BLOCKER] The platform never states an indication, a patient population, or a target product profile, which makes target validation formally undefined and every efficacy and safety number unfalsifiable — There is no answer in the repository to the first question any target-validation exercise must answer: which disease, in which patients, measured how. Alzheimer's disease, mild cognitive impairment, and cognitive enhancement in healthy adults are three different indications with three different genetic architectures, three different regulatory paths, three different acceptable benefit-risk ratios, and three different sets of validated targets. Without a declared indication no target-disease association score can be computed at all — the Open Targets query I ran required an ontology term (MONDO_0004975) that I had to supply myself because the platform supplies none. The 25 'targeted therapeutics' are therefore untargeted in the only sense that matters: they have no declared therapeutic target population. Consequence: Two concrete decision failures follow. First, the safety bar is undefined and therefore unmeetable: the platform's blanket 'hERG IC50 > 50 μM (0% Risk)' and 'Tolerance Downregulation < 4.2% after 30 days' (README.md:99-102) would be a plausible discussion in severe, rapidly fatal AD and an outright non-starter for chronic dosing of cognitively healthy adults, where any oncogenic or seizure liability is disqualifying. A reader cannot tell which case is being argued. Second, the genetic architecture differs by indication and drives target choice: AD risk is dominated by APOE and microglial loci (Bellenguez 2022), whereas cognitive-function and educational-attainment GWAS are massively polygenic with tiny per-locus effects and essentially no tractable single-target hits — so 'cognitive enhancement' as framed here has no genetics-supported target list to draw from. Presenting a hippocampus/PFC/basal-forebrain anatomy map as if it were an indication conceals that gap.

text: Required fix for GENO-02: Add a Target Product Profile section to README.md and a TPP panel to index.html, before the candidate list, containing: indication with EFO/MONDO ID; population and stage with biomarker inclusion criteria; primary/secondary clinical endpoints; comparator; target engagement biomarker; route and chronic-dosing duration; and a maximum acceptable risk statement. Then re-derive every target-disease association against that declared ontology term and show the score in the UI. Separately, relabel all efficacy percentages with the exact assay, species, model, n, comparator, and citation — or, if they are hypothesised rather than measured, move them into a clearly marked 'design target (not measured)' field. If the intent is healthy cognitive enhancement rather than a disease, state that explicitly and add the corresponding regulatory framing, because it changes the acceptable safety profile more than any other single decision in the project.

tags: Human genetics & genomics — therapeutic target validation (GWAS, Mendelian randomization, QTL colocalization, population constraint)
text: Ground truth for GENO-02: A target product profile is the standard artefact that fixes this, and at minimum must specify: (i) indication with an ontology identifier (e.g. MONDO_0004975 Alzheimer disease, or MONDO_0005071/EFO term for MCI) rather than an anatomical region; (ii) the patient population and stage, with biomarker-defined inclusion (amyloid-PET or CSF Aβ42/40 and p-tau217 positivity is the current standard for AD trials) and, where genetics defines the mechanism, genotype-based stratification; (iii) primary and key secondary clinical endpoints (CDR-SB, ADAS-Cog13, ADCS-ADL) plus target-engagement and disease-progression biomarkers; (iv) comparator and expected effect size on the clinical scale, not a percentage change in an in-vitro or rodent readout; (v) route, regimen, and duration of exposure; (vi) an explicit maximum acceptable risk tied to the population. Minikel et al. 2024 (DOI 10.1038/s41586-024-07316-0) also shows the genetic-support advantage is computed per target-INDICATION pair, not per target — so an undeclared indication makes the strongest available prior on success uncomputable in principle, not merely unreported.

text: [CRITICAL] Human genetics points the wrong way for four target programmes: the platform proposes GluN2A potentiation, TrkA/TrkB agonism, Keap1 inhibition/Nrf2 activation, and GSK-3β inhibition while declaring them safe, when the corresponding human genetic evidence is epilepsy, oncogenic kinase fusion, and oncogenic driver mutation — Each of these four programmes runs against, not with, the direction indicated by human genetics, and in each case the platform asserts safety on exactly the axis the genetics flags. (1) GRIN2A. Open Targets, top genetic_association scores across all diseases: Landau-Kleffner syndrome 0.95, hereditary disease 0.88, Seizure 0.85, Rolandic epilepsy 0.84, developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 0.66. gnomAD v4: pLI 1.0000, LOEUF 0.277, observed 22 LoF against 113.4 expected (81% depletion). GRIN2A is the archetypal human epilepsy gene; both loss- and gain-of-function variants cause seizure disorders. Declaring 'Excitotoxicity: Safe' for a GluN2A potentiator with a 'Capped Emax 135%' is asserting the absence of the exact phenotype human genetics predicts. There is also no genetic_association evidence linking GRIN2A to AD at all — its AD score of 0.623 is carried by 'clinical' 0.988 (memantine-class drugs). (2) NTRK1/NTRK2 agonism. TRK receptors are proto-oncogenes; the approved human pharmacology is inhibition, not agonism (Drilon et al., NEJM 378:731-739, 2018). Open Targets confirms the direction: NTRK2 non-small-cell lung carcinoma clinical score 0.95, neoplasm 0.739 with somatic_mutation 0.46; NTRK1 NSCLC clinical 0.95, melanoma somatic 0.61. NTRK2 is also among the most LoF-intolerant genes in the genome (pLI 1.0000, LOEUF 0.219, 13 observed vs 94.5 expected LoF, 86% depletion) and its own human genetic phenotypes are obesity/hyperphagia/developmental delay (genetic 0.83) and developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (0.80) — not AD (genetic 0.080). NTRK1 LoF causes HSAN type IV / CIPA (genetic 0.94). (3) Keap1 inhibition / Nrf2 activation. This is the best-documented case in the set. Open Targets somatic_mutation scores: KEAP1 in lung adenocarcinoma 0.80, NSCLC 0.71, lung carcinoma 0.61, hepatocellular carcinoma 0.60; NFE2L2 in HCC 0.77, head-and-neck SCC 0.66, esophageal SCC 0.61. KEAP1 LoF and NFE2L2 GoF are recurrent somatic oncogenic drivers that produce exactly the constitutive Nrf2 activation the platform is engineering. Critically, the germline experiment has also been done in humans: Huppke et al., Nat Commun 8:818 (2017) report that de novo NFE2L2 activating mutations — 'the same mutations' found somatically in cancer — cause an early-onset multisystem disorder with failure to thrive, immunodeficiency and neurological symptoms. Neither KEAP1 (AD overall 0.088) nor NFE2L2 (0.120) has any genetic_association evidence for AD. (4) GSK-3β inhibition. The platform's own Pathway 03 diagram (index.html:242-257) traces GSK-3β inhibition to β-catenin stabilization, TCF/LEF activation and cyclin D1 transcription — the canonical Wnt oncogenic axis — and presents it as a therapeutic outcome with no oncogenicity discussion. GSK3B is highly constrained (gnomAD v4 pLI 0.9999, LOEUF 0.409, 15 observed vs 56.4 expected LoF) and has no genetic_association with AD; its 0.554 AD score is literature 0.965 plus affected_pathway 0.84. Consequence: These are not conservative errors. Each proposes chronic systemic modulation of a pathway whose human genetic signature is cancer or epilepsy, and each attaches a fabricated safety metric asserting that risk is zero. A reader with a pharmacology background but no genetics background — the likely audience for a 'cognition enhancement' platform — would take 'Tumorigenicity: Negligible' (app.js:177) and 'Excitotoxicity: Safe' (app.js:219) at face value and prioritise these candidates. The Keap1/Nrf2 case is the most consequential because the platform builds three separate candidates on it (X3, M2, M5) and because chronic Nrf2 activation in a population with elevated cancer incidence is precisely the scenario the somatic and germline genetics warn against; Huppke 2017 removes the usual objection that somatic driver evidence does not transfer to germline/pharmacological activation. The GRIN2A case matters because the claimed safety margin is stated numerically ('Seizure Index 0.02') with no derivation, in a target class where human LoF and GoF variants both produce seizure phenotypes.

text: Required fix for GENO-03: Add a mandatory direction-of-effect and genetic-safety field to every candidate record in FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA (app.js:138-398), populated from data rather than asserted, containing: (a) intended direction (agonism/antagonism/inhibition/potentiation); (b) the human allelic series for that target and which direction each class of variant moves disease risk; (c) gnomAD v4 pLI/LOEUF; (d) Open Targets somatic_mutation scores across oncology indications; (e) an explicit oncogenicity and seizure-liability assessment derived from (b)-(d). Then act on the output: for GRIN2A, either drop the programme or replace 'Excitotoxicity: Safe' with the epilepsy allelic series and a derived, defensible margin; for NTRK1/NTRK2 agonism, add the TRK-fusion oncogenicity risk explicitly and justify agonism against approved inhibitor pharmacology, or reframe as a non-catalytic/biased mechanism with evidence; for Keap1/Nrf2 (X3, M2, M5), add the KEAP1 lung-adenocarcinoma somatic score 0.80, the NFE2L2 HCC score 0.77 and Huppke 2017 to the safety panel and state a chronic-dosing cancer-risk position, since three of 25 candidates depend on it; for GSK-3β, annotate index.html:254 with the Wnt/β-catenin/cyclin D1 oncogenic liability instead of presenting it as a clean therapeutic outcome. Delete every hardcoded safety string that asserts a value the platform did not compute ('Tumorigenicity: Negligible' app.js:177, 'Excitotoxicity: Safe' app.js:219, 'Off-target Binding: None' app.js:209, 'Cytokine Storm Risk: 0%' app.js:323, 'Fibril Blockade: 100%' app.js:281, 'Safety Plasticity Score: 99.5 / 100' app.js:291, 'Safety Index: 99.1 / 100' app.js:343).

tags: Human genetics & genomics — therapeutic target validation (GWAS, Mendelian randomization, QTL colocalization, population constraint)
text: Ground truth for GENO-03: Direction of effect is the central inference in genetics-informed target validation: a target is validated for a mechanism only when the human allelic series shows that moving the target in the intended direction moves disease risk in the intended direction, and the safety case is read off the phenotypes of humans who already carry variants of the opposite sign. Key references, all retrieved and verified: Karczewski et al., Nature 581:434-443 (2020), DOI 10.1038/s41586-020-2308-7 — gnomAD constraint framework; LoF-intolerant genes (low LOEUF, high pLI) are those where partial inactivation is not phenotypically free, and the same logic bounds how far a target can be pharmacologically pushed. Drilon et al., NEJM 378:731-739 (2018), DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa1714448 — larotrectinib, 'a highly selective TRK inhibitor', in TRK fusion-positive cancers; the validated human TRK pharmacology is inhibition. Huppke et al., Nat Commun 8:818 (2017), DOI 10.1038/s41467-017-00932-7 — 'Somatic mutations of NFE2L2 leading to NRF2 accumulation promote cell survival and drug resistance in cancer cells. Here we show that the same mutations as inborn de novo mutations cause an early onset multisystem disorder with failure to thrive, immunodeficiency and neurological symptoms.' Cai et al., Int J Cancer 144:788-801 (2019), DOI 10.1002/ijc.31975 — KEAP1/NRF2-mutant lung cancers show impaired angiogenesis, elevated hypoxic stress and deficient immune-cell infiltrates, i.e. the pathway alteration reshapes the tumour microenvironment. Open Targets Platform (Ochoa et al., Nucleic Acids Res 51:D1353-D1359, 2023, DOI 10.1093/nar/gkac1046) supplies the somatic_mutation, genetic_association and clinical datatype scores quoted above.

tags: Human genetics & genomics — therapeutic target validation (GWAS, Mendelian randomization, QTL colocalization, population constraint)
text: [MAJOR] The '5 brain regions / cell-type targeted' organising claim rests on no expression evidence, and GTEx contradicts it for at least four of the targets — The platform assigns each candidate to a brain region and cell type by narrative assertion, never by expression data, and in four cases the assertion is contradicted by the reference human expression atlas. AstroEos-NO-A1 (app.js:349-356) claims to act on 'Astrocytes & Brain Microvascular Endothelial Cells' via eNOS and promises 'Cerebral Blood Flow (CBF) +45%' with 'Vasodilation Rate: Safe (+45%)' — but NOS3 median expression is 17.6-fold higher in spleen than in cortex, so a systemically administered eNOS stimulator engages peripheral vasculature far more than cerebral vasculature, and the safety statement addresses only the cerebral effect. AstroPafr-Block-A4 (app.js:379-386) targets PTAFR on 'Cerebral Capillaries & Astrocytic Endfeet' — PTAFR is 57-fold higher in whole blood than in cortex; it is a myeloid/platelet gene, and the dominant in-vivo pharmacology of a PAFR antagonist will be haematological, not neurovascular. HippoNrf-KeapDecoy-X3 and PfcGsk-WntLinker-P4 are assigned to hippocampal CA1 neurons and PFC dendritic spines respectively, but KEAP1 and GSK3B are ubiquitously expressed with no CNS enrichment whatsoever, so there is no expression basis for regional selectivity — the 'targeting' is a label, not a property. Separately, CHRNA7 (app.js:193-200, PfcACh-PAM-P1) cannot be assessed from bulk RNA-seq at all without addressing CHRFAM7A (ENSG00000166664, annotated in Open Targets as 'CHRNA7 (exons 5-10) and FAM7A (exons A-E) fusion'), the human-specific partial-duplication paralog at 15q13.3 that confounds read mapping and acts as a dominant-negative on α7 assembly; the platform's bulk-level Brain-Cortex value of 0.3 TPM is uninterpretable without that correction, and the 15q13.3 CNV locus (MONDO_0012774) is never mentioned. Consequence: The five-region map is the platform's main interpretive frame — it is the second navigation tab, the ASCII figure in the README, and the organising key for all 25 candidates — so a reader takes cellular selectivity as established. It is not. Two candidates (A1, A4) are assigned to a cellular compartment where their target is a minority of total body expression, which means the predicted in-vivo pharmacology and the peripheral safety profile are both wrong, and the safety strings ('Vasodilation Rate: Safe (+45%)' app.js:355; 'Cerebral Edema: Prevented' app.js:385) discuss only the intended compartment. Two more (X3, P4) claim regional action on ubiquitously expressed targets, which is the classic source of on-target peripheral toxicity for systemically dosed agents. The genuinely brain-enriched targets in the set — SLC1A2, CHRM1, GRIN2A — get no credit for it, because the platform never distinguished them.

text: Required fix for GENO-04: Replace the asserted region/cell-type fields with fetched data. (1) For every target, pull GTEx median TPM across all 54 tissues and store, at minimum, brain-region values plus the maximum non-brain tissue and the resulting CNS/periphery ratio; render this in the drug modal next to the 'targets' field so the reader sees NOS3 spleen 75.5 vs cortex 4.3 rather than 'CNS -> Brain -> Astrocytes'. (2) Add single-nucleus brain expression to justify each cell-type assignment (neuron vs astrocyte vs microglia vs endothelium); bulk GTEx cannot support the astrocyte and BMEC claims at app.js:353, 363, 383. (3) Add Human Protein Atlas protein-level localisation. (4) For any target whose CNS/periphery ratio is below ~1, add an explicit on-target peripheral liability statement — this applies to NOS3, PTAFR, KEAP1, GSK3B and arguably ACHE. (5) For CHRNA7, either exclude it or add explicit CHRFAM7A-aware quantification and a note on the 15q13.3 CNV; do not report a bulk CHRNA7 TPM without that caveat. (6) Where expression contradicts the assigned region (A1, A4), either re-assign the candidate or withdraw the regional claim. All of this is achievable with the .agents/skills/gtex-database and human-protein-atlas-database scripts already vendored in the repo.

tags: Human genetics & genomics — therapeutic target validation (GWAS, Mendelian randomization, QTL colocalization, population constraint)
text: Ground truth for GENO-04: Cell-type specificity is an evidence claim requiring expression data, and for a CNS programme it requires single-cell/single-nucleus resolution, because bulk brain tissue averages over neurons, astrocytes, microglia, oligodendrocytes and endothelium — the exact distinctions this platform's five-region map depends on. The standard evidence stack is: bulk cross-tissue expression (GTEx v8/v10, gtexportal.org/api/v2, to establish CNS versus peripheral partition and therefore on-target peripheral liability); protein-level tissue and subcellular localisation (Human Protein Atlas); and single-nucleus brain atlases for cell-type assignment. The relevance of doing this properly for AD specifically is established by Bellenguez et al., Nat Genet 54:412-436 (2022), DOI 10.1038/s41588-022-01024-z, whose pathway enrichment across 75 risk loci 'confirmed the involvement of amyloid/tau pathways and highlighted microglia implication' — i.e. the cell type is itself a genetics-derived finding, not an anatomical assumption. Karczewski et al., Nature 581:434-443 (2020), DOI 10.1038/s41586-020-2308-7 supplies the complementary constraint layer.

tags: Human genetics & genomics — therapeutic target validation (GWAS, Mendelian randomization, QTL colocalization, population constraint)
text: [MAJOR] TREM2 is the one genetically validated target and the agonist direction is right, but the platform names Arg47 — the R47H Alzheimer's risk residue — as a drug binding site with no stratification plan and no awareness of what that residue is — The scientific target choice here is correct and I want to be clear about that: partial loss of TREM2 function raises AD risk, so TREM2 agonism is the right direction, and microglia are the cell type AD genetics actually implicates. But the platform arrived at the correct answer without the genetics, and the cost shows in the detail. Arg47 is listed as one of three receptor binding residues for the agonist — and Arg47 is the position of rs75932628 (p.Arg47His), the rare coding variant that defines TREM2's status as a genetically validated AD target (Jonsson: OR 2.92, 95% CI 2.09-4.09, P = 3.42x10^-10 in Iceland; combined OR 2.90, P = 2.1x10^-12). R47H sits in the ligand-binding surface of the TREM2 Ig-like domain and impairs ligand engagement, which is the mechanistic basis for its risk effect. So the platform is claiming Kd = 0.52 nM against a binding surface whose most important human variant alters that exact residue, in the population that variant defines, and says nothing about it. There is no statement of whether the agonist is intended for R47H carriers or for wild-type TREM2, no discussion of whether R47H would abolish or preserve binding, no genotype-stratified development plan, and no acknowledgement that biallelic TREM2 LoF causes Nasu-Hakola disease (OT genetic 0.89) — which bounds how much TREM2 function can be lost but also tells you what the receptor does. The Kd is in any case a fabricated constant, not a computed value (see the hardcoded FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA array). Consequence: This determines who the drug is for and whether the trial can succeed. If the agonist binds the Arg47 pocket, R47H carriers — the very population with the strongest genetic rationale for TREM2 agonism — may be the population in which the drug does not bind. That is a recruitment and stratification decision that must be made before candidate selection, not after a failed Phase II. Conversely, if the intent is to rescue R47H-associated hypofunction, the candidate must be shown to engage the R47H variant receptor, which requires designing against both alleles. At ~0.3% allele frequency the carrier population is small enough that enrichment strategies are mandatory and large enough that unstratified trials will be diluted. Getting this wrong is the single most likely way a genetically well-chosen target still fails in the clinic, and it is exactly the failure mode the genetics layer exists to prevent.

tags: Human genetics & genomics — therapeutic target validation (GWAS, Mendelian randomization, QTL colocalization, population constraint)
text: Required fix for GENO-05: Add a genetic-variant and stratification block to the TREM2 candidates (app.js:297-304 and app.js:337-344) containing: (1) rs75932628 / p.Arg47His with its gnomAD v4 allele frequencies (exome AF 0.002855, genome AF 0.001996) and the Jonsson/Guerreiro odds ratios and confidence intervals; (2) an explicit statement of whether the agonist is designed for wild-type TREM2, for R47H TREM2, or for both, with binding data or predictions for each allele — this is required precisely because the platform itself names Arg47 as a contact residue; (3) the Nasu-Hakola recessive-LoF phenotype as the lower bound on tolerable TREM2 function; (4) a genotype-stratified development plan naming the enrichment strategy and, if R47H carriers are the intended population, the screening assay. More generally, add a ClinVar and gnomAD variant panel to every target card (the .agents/skills/clinvar-database, gnomad-database and dbsnp-database skills are already vendored) so that any coding variant falling in a claimed binding site is surfaced automatically rather than discovered in the clinic. Finally, replace the hardcoded 'Kd = 0.52 nM' with either a computed value plus method or an explicit 'not measured' label.

tags: Human genetics & genomics — therapeutic target validation (GWAS, Mendelian randomization, QTL colocalization, population constraint)
text: Ground truth for GENO-05: Guerreiro et al., N Engl J Med 368:117-27 (2013), DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa1211851: 'Heterozygous rare variants in TREM2 are associated with a significant increase in the risk of Alzheimer's disease'; the most commonly associated variant is rs75932628 (R47H), and 'Homozygous loss-of-function mutations in TREM2 … have previously been associated with an autosomal recessive form of early-onset dementia' (Nasu-Hakola). Jonsson et al., N Engl J Med 368:107-16 (2013), DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa1211103: rs75932628-T confers OR 2.92 (95% CI 2.09-4.09, P = 3.42x10^-10) in Iceland, OR 2.90 (P = 2.1x10^-12) combined; frequency 0.46% in controls aged 85+; carriers aged 80-100 without AD had poorer cognitive function than non-carriers (P = 0.003); the authors attribute the effect to 'impaired containment of inflammatory processes' — i.e. reduced TREM2 function raises risk, which is what licenses agonism. Bellenguez et al., Nat Genet 54:412-436 (2022), DOI 10.1038/s41588-022-01024-z independently confirms microglia as the AD-implicated cell type across 75 loci. Constraint context from Karczewski et al., Nature 581:434-443 (2020), DOI 10.1038/s41586-020-2308-7: TREM2's LOEUF of 1.268 places it among LoF-tolerant genes, consistent with a recessive disease gene and with the modest per-allele effect of heterozygous R47H.

tags: Human genetics & genomics — therapeutic target validation (GWAS, Mendelian randomization, QTL colocalization, population constraint)
text: The support of human genetic evidence for approved drug indications (2015). The original quantification of the genetics-to-approval relationship: direct genetic support rises from 2.0% of mechanisms at preclinical to 8.2% among approved mechanisms, and 'selecting genetically supported targets could double the success rate in clinical development.' Application here: Establishes the baseline expectation that a drug discovery platform performs target-indication genetic triage before committing to 25 candidates. Supplies the 2x figure the platform's target selection forfeits for 16 of 17 targets.

tags: Human genetics & genomics — therapeutic target validation (GWAS, Mendelian randomization, QTL colocalization, population constraint)
text: Are drug targets with genetic support twice as likely to be approved? Revised estimates of the impact of genetic support for drug mechanisms on the probability of drug approval (2019). Independent replication and refinement of Nelson 2015 with regression adjustment for target and indication properties; finds >2-fold increase in approval when the causal gene is clear (Mendelian traits, coding-variant GWAS associations), and shows the Mendelian association holds prospectively. Application here: Defines the evidence tier the platform should be aiming for — coding-variant or Mendelian-grade causal-gene assignment, which is exactly the tier TREM2/rs75932628 occupies and which none of the other 16 targets reaches for a cognition indication.

tags: Human genetics & genomics — therapeutic target validation (GWAS, Mendelian randomization, QTL colocalization, population constraint)
text: Refining the impact of genetic evidence on clinical success (2024). Current best estimate: probability of success for genetically supported mechanisms is 2.6x greater than for unsupported ones; the advantage improves with confidence in the causal gene and is largely independent of genetic effect size, minor allele frequency, or year of discovery. Application here: Supplies the multiplier for the portfolio arithmetic in GENO-01 (≈18.6% vs ≈7.1% per programme at a 10% base rate). The finding that effect size and MAF do not matter is directly relevant: the platform cannot dismiss TREM2-grade rare-variant evidence as too small to act on, nor claim credit for mechanism plausibility in its absence.

tags: Human genetics & genomics — therapeutic target validation (GWAS, Mendelian randomization, QTL colocalization, population constraint)
text: The mutational constraint spectrum quantified from variation in 141,456 humans (2020). The gnomAD constraint framework (pLI, o/e LoF, LOEUF) classifying protein-coding genes along a spectrum of tolerance to inactivation, validated against model-organism and cell-line essentiality data. Application here: Provides the safety prior the platform never computes. Applied here it separates targets where partial inhibition is not phenotypically free (NTRK2 LOEUF 0.219, GRIN2A 0.277, CHRM1 0.332, GSK3B 0.409) from LoF-tolerant targets where human carriers already demonstrate the consequence (TREM2 LOEUF 1.268, PTAFR 0.982, NTRK1 0.882, NOS3 0.800).

tags: Human genetics & genomics — therapeutic target validation (GWAS, Mendelian randomization, QTL colocalization, population constraint)
text: TREM2 variants in Alzheimer's disease (2013). Sequencing of 1,092 AD cases and 1,107 controls plus GWAS meta-analysis and a 1,887-case/4,061-control replication, establishing that heterozygous rare TREM2 exon-2 variants, principally rs75932628 (R47H), significantly increase AD risk; notes that homozygous TREM2 LoF causes recessive early-onset dementia (Nasu-Hakola). Application here: The genetic validation for the platform's one defensible target, and the source of the Arg47/R47H residue conflict in GENO-05. Also supplies the recessive-LoF lower bound on tolerable TREM2 function that the safety string at app.js:303 omits.

tags: Human genetics & genomics — therapeutic target validation (GWAS, Mendelian randomization, QTL colocalization, population constraint)
text: Variant of TREM2 associated with the risk of Alzheimer's disease (2013). deCODE whole-genome-based discovery of rs75932628-T (R47H): OR 2.92 (95% CI 2.09-4.09, P = 3.42x10^-10) in Iceland, OR 2.90 (P = 2.1x10^-12) combined with US/Norwegian/Dutch/German replication; frequency 0.46% in controls aged 85+; non-demented carriers aged 80-100 show poorer cognition (P = 0.003); attributes risk to impaired containment of inflammatory processes. Application here: Establishes the direction of effect that licenses TREM2 agonism (reduced function raises risk) and the effect size and allele frequency needed for the genotype-stratified development plan required in GENO-05.

tags: Human genetics & genomics — therapeutic target validation (GWAS, Mendelian randomization, QTL colocalization, population constraint)
text: Activating de novo mutations in NFE2L2 encoding NRF2 cause a multisystem disorder (2017). Demonstrates that the same NFE2L2 activating mutations found somatically in cancer, when present as inborn de novo germline variants, cause early-onset multisystem disease with failure to thrive, immunodeficiency and neurological symptoms, via NRF2 accumulation and cytosolic redox imbalance. Application here: The decisive human-genetics safety evidence against the platform's three Keap1-inhibitor / Nrf2-activator candidates (X3 app.js:161-168, M2 app.js:307-314, M5 app.js:337-344). It closes the usual escape route that somatic cancer-driver evidence does not transfer to pharmacological activation: the germline experiment has been done and produces a disease phenotype.

tags: Human genetics & genomics — therapeutic target validation (GWAS, Mendelian randomization, QTL colocalization, population constraint)
text: Clinicopathological, microenvironmental and genetic determinants of molecular subtypes in KEAP1/NRF2-mutant lung cancer (2018). Characterisation of somatic KEAP1/NFE2L2-pathway-altered lung adenocarcinomas and squamous cell carcinomas: APOBEC mutational signatures, impaired tumour angiogenesis, elevated hypoxic stress and deficient immune-cell infiltrates. Application here: Corroborates the Open Targets somatic_mutation scores I retrieved (KEAP1 lung adenocarcinoma 0.80, NSCLC 0.71; NFE2L2 HCC 0.77) and shows that constitutive NRF2 activation is not merely a passenger but reshapes the tumour microenvironment — the risk that must be stated for chronic Nrf2-activating therapy.

tags: Human genetics & genomics — therapeutic target validation (GWAS, Mendelian randomization, QTL colocalization, population constraint)
text: Efficacy of Larotrectinib in TRK Fusion-Positive Cancers in Adults and Children (2018). Pivotal evidence for larotrectinib, 'a highly selective TRK inhibitor', across TRK fusion-positive cancers in adults and children — the basis of the approved, tumour-agnostic human TRK pharmacology. Application here: Establishes that the validated human TRK pharmacology is inhibition, not agonism, which is the direction-of-effect conflict for the platform's TrkB and TrkA agonist candidates (X1 app.js:141-148, B3 app.js:265-272, and the NTRK2-directed AF3 candidates at app.js:125-128). Corroborated by Open Targets clinical scores of 0.95 for both NTRK1 and NTRK2 in NSCLC.

tags: Human genetics & genomics — therapeutic target validation (GWAS, Mendelian randomization, QTL colocalization, population constraint)
text: New insights into the genetic etiology of Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (2022). Two-stage GWAS of 111,326 clinically diagnosed/proxy AD cases and 677,663 controls identifying 75 risk loci (42 new), with 31 newly prioritized genes; pathway enrichment confirms amyloid/tau involvement and highlights microglia; includes a genetic risk score predicting MCI-to-AD progression. Application here: The reference genetic architecture the platform's target list should have been triaged against. It supplies both the credit (microglia and TREM2 are genetically the right place to work) and the indictment (none of ACHE, GSK3B, KEAP1, NFE2L2, FZD8, CHRNA7, GRIN2A, SLC1A2, PTAFR, CHRM1, NTRK1 sits in a prioritized AD locus). Its MCI-progression risk score is also directly relevant to the population definition missing in GENO-02.

tags: Human genetics & genomics — therapeutic target validation (GWAS, Mendelian randomization, QTL colocalization, population constraint)
text: The next-generation Open Targets Platform: reimagined, redesigned, rebuilt (2023). The open-source target identification and prioritisation resource with harmonised gene-disease causal evidence across rare, common and somatic disease, plus target safety and tractability annotations including genetic constraint, PROTACtability and AlphaFold structures. Application here: The exact tool the repo vendors as .agents/skills/opentargets-database and never calls. All association scores and datatype breakdowns quoted in my findings came from its GraphQL API in this session; wiring it in as a build-time fetch is the single highest-leverage fix for GENO-01, and its constraint and tractability annotations also address parts of GENO-03 and GENO-04.
